'''Mason Christopher Jones''' (born July 21, 1998) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Hong Kong Bulls]] of the Chinese [[National Basketball League (China)|National Basketball League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Connors State College|Connors State Cowboys]] and the [[Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball|Arkansas Razorbacks]]. He debuted in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) in 2020, playing since then for the [[Houston Rockets]], [[Philadelphia 76ers]], [[Los Angeles Lakers]] and [[Sacramento Kings]]. In 2025, he helped the [[Stockton Kings]] win the [[List of NBA G League champions|NBA G League champion]] behind his [[NBA G League Finals MVP|Finals MVP]] performance.

==Early life==
Jones grew up in [[DeSoto, Texas]] and did not play basketball until his senior year of high school at [[Triple A Academy]] in [[Dallas, Texas]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.arkansasonline.com/news/2018/apr/11/razorbacks-basketball-team-sign-juco-player-today/|title=Razorbacks basketball team to sign juco player today|first=Richard|last=Davenport|work=[[Arkansas Democrat-Gazette]]|date=April 11, 2018|access-date=February 2, 2020}}</ref> That year, he averaged 15.9 points, 5.7 rebounds, and 4.1 assists per game.<ref>{{cite web |last=Allen |first=Nate |date=December 16, 2019 |title=Razorbacks Basketball: Mason Jones recovers against Tulsa |url=https://www.swtimes.com/sports/20191216/razorbacks-basketball-mason-jones-recovers-against-tulsa |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191217220214/https://www.swtimes.com/sports/20191216/razorbacks-basketball-mason-jones-recovers-against-tulsa |archive-date=December 17, 2019 |access-date=February 2, 2020 |work=[[Southwest Times Record]]}}</ref> Jones played at Link Year Prep in [[Branson, Missouri]] for a [[postgraduate year]], trimming his weight down from 265 pounds from his senior year of high school to 230 by the end of the season.<ref name="family friend"/>

==College career==
[[File:Mason Jones.jpg|thumb|Jones with [[Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball|Arkansas]] in 2019]]
Jones played his freshman season at [[Connors State College]]. He averaged 15.5 points, 6.9 rebounds and 2.5 assists per game in his only season for the Cowboys.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/college/arkansas/Article/Arkansas-Razorbacks-signee-Mason-Jones-comes-from-a-basketball-family--118380676/|title=Arkansas signee Mason Jones from strong basketball bloodline|first=Tyler|last=Davis|website=247Sports.com|date=May 20, 2018|access-date=February 2, 2020}}</ref> Jones committed to transfer to Arkansas following the end of the season over offers from [[BYU Cougars men's basketball|BYU]] and [[Washington Huskies men's basketball|Washington]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.arkansasfight.com/2018/4/8/17212544/mason-jones-commits-to-arkansas|title=Mason Jones Commits to Arkansas|first=Eric|last=Harris|website=ArkansasFight.com|publisher=[[SB Nation]]|date=April 8, 2018|access-date=February 2, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.wholehogsports.com/news/2018/apr/07/connors-state-standout-mason-jones-commits-arkansa/|title=Connors State standout Mason Jones discusses commitment to Arkansas|first=Dudley E.|last=Dawson|website=WholeHogSports.com|date=April 7, 2018|access-date=February 2, 2020}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Houston Rockets (2020–2021)===
After going undrafted in the [[2020 NBA draft]], Jones signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Houston Rockets]] on November 26, 2020.<ref>{{cite web|title=Rockets Announce Roster Additions|url=https://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-announce-roster-additions|work=NBA.com|date=November 26, 2020|access-date=November 26, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first=Brian|last=Bennett|title=Mason Jones reportedly signs with Rockets: Here's what they're getting|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/2168795/2020/11/19/mason-jones-reportedly-signs-with-rockets-heres-what-theyre-getting/|website=[[The Athletic]]|date=November 19, 2020|access-date=November 19, 2020}}</ref> He was waived on March 8, 2021.<ref>{{cite web|title=Rockets Sign Anthony Lamb to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-sign-anthony-lamb-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=March 8, 2021|access-date=March 8, 2021}}</ref> On March 12, he signed a 10-day contract with the Rockets.<ref>{{cite web|title=Rockets Sign Mason Jones to 10-Day Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-sign-mason-jones-10-day-contract|website=NBA.com|date=March 12, 2021|access-date=March 12, 2021}}</ref> He appeared in 26 games for the Rockets during the [[2020–21 Houston Rockets season|2020–21 season]].<ref name=br21>{{cite web |title=Mason Jones 2020-21 Game Log |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/j/jonesma05/gamelog/2021/ |website=Basketball-Reference.com |access-date=5 September 2025 |language=en}}</ref>

===Philadelphia 76ers (2021)===
On March 26, 2021, Jones signed a two-way contract with the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].<ref>{{cite web|title=76ers Sign Paul Reed to Standard NBA Contract, Mason Jones to Two-Way Deal|url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/76ers-sign-paul-reed-standard-nba-contract-mason-jones-two-way-deal|website=NBA.com|date=March 26, 2021|access-date=March 26, 2021}}</ref> On May 6, he was waived by the 76ers.<ref>{{cite tweet|author=((Philadelphia 76ers))|number=1390399892447711233|title=We have waived Mason Jones.|user=sixers|date=May 6, 2021|access-date=May 8, 2021}}</ref> He appeared in four games for the 76ers.<ref name="br21" />

Jones played for the [[Washington Wizards]] in the [[2021 NBA Summer League]].<ref name=realgm>{{cite web |title=Mason Jones Player Profile, Sacramento Kings - RealGM |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/player/Mason-Jones/Summary/131612 |website=basketball.realgm.com |access-date=5 September 2025 |language=en}}</ref>

===South Bay / Los Angeles Lakers (2021–2022)===
On November 6, 2021, Jones was acquired by the [[South Bay Lakers]] of the [[NBA G League]].<ref>{{cite tweet|author=South Bay Lakers|number=1457069345264136193|title=The #SBLakers have acquired Mason Jones from the @LakelandMagic in exchange for a first-round pick in the 2022 @nbagleague Draft. In a related move, the team has waived Daishon Smith.|user=SouthBayLakers|date=November 6, 2021|access-date=November 15, 2021}}</ref>

On December 21, 2021, after 12 games with South Bay, Jones signed a two-way contract with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].<ref name="LAL2w">{{cite web|title=Lakers Waive Chaundee Brown Jr., Sign Mason Jones to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/lakers-waive-chaundee-brown-jr-sign-mason-jones-to-two-way-contract-2021|website=NBA.com|date=December 21, 2021|access-date=December 21, 2021}}</ref> He played four games for Los Angeles over the rest of the [[2021–22 Los Angeles Lakers season|2021–22 season]],<ref>{{cite web |title=Mason Jones 2021-22 Game Log |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/j/jonesma05/gamelog/2022/ |website=Basketball-Reference.com |access-date=5 September 2025 |language=en}}</ref> and finished the [[2021–22 NBA G League season]] with 40 games for South Bay.<ref name="realgm" />

Jones played for the Los Angeles Lakers in the [[2022 NBA Summer League]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Lakers Announce 2022 Summer League Roster {{!}} Los Angeles Lakers |url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/news/lakers-announce-2022-summer-league-roster |access-date=5 September 2025 |work=www.nba.com |date=28 June 2022 |language=en}}</ref>

===Mexico City Capitanes (2022–2023)===
On October 11, 2022, Jones was acquired by the [[Mexico City Capitanes]] of the NBA G League.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://capitanes.gleague.nba.com/news/capitanes-acquire-returning-player-rights-to-mason-jones|title=Capitanes acquire returning player rights to Mason Jones|date=October 11, 2022|website=NBA.com|access-date=October 11, 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://capitanes.mx/capitanes-anuncia-roster-training-camp-2022-23|title=Capitanes anuncia roster para el training camp 2022-23|language=ES|date=November 4, 2022|website=capitanes.mx|access-date=November 4, 2022}}</ref> He appeared in 38 games for the Capitanes during the [[2022–23 NBA G League season]].<ref name="realgm" />

===Darüşşafaka Lassa (2023)===
On July 16, 2023, Jones signed with [[Darüşşafaka Basketbol|Darüşşafaka Lassa]] of the [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]] (BSL).<ref>{{cite web|first=Ahmet Melık|last=Subaşi|title=Hoş Geldin Mason Jones!|url=https://darussafakabasketbol.com/hos-geldin-mason-jones/|website=DarussafakaBasketbol.com|date=July 16, 2023|access-date=July 16, 2023|language=Turkish}}</ref> He appeared in five BSL games and three [[Basketball Champions League|BCL]] games to start the [[2023–24 Basketbol Süper Ligi|2023–24 season]].<ref name=Eurobasket>{{cite web |title=Mason Jones |url=https://basketball.asia-basket.com/player/Mason-Jones/458750 |website=Eurobasket LLC |access-date=14 January 2026 |url-access=subscription}}</ref>

===Sacramento / Stockton Kings (2023–2025)===
On December 8, 2023, Jones was acquired by the [[Stockton Kings]] of the NBA G League.<ref>{{cite web|title=Stockton Kings Announce Three Team Trade|url=https://stockton.gleague.nba.com/news/stockton-kings-announce-three-team-trade|website=NBA.com|date=December 8, 2023|access-date=December 14, 2023}}</ref> On February 9, 2024, he signed a two-way contract with the [[Sacramento Kings]].<ref>{{cite tweet|first=James|last=Ham|title=Kings officially announce the signing of Mason Jones to a two-way contract.|number=1756147155893727343|user=James_HamNBA|date=February 9, 2024|access-date=February 9, 2024}}</ref> He appeared in five games for Sacramento to finish the [[2023–24 Sacramento Kings season|2023–24 season]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Mason Jones 2023-24 Game Log |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/j/jonesma05/gamelog/2024/ |website=Basketball-Reference.com |access-date=5 September 2025 |language=en}}</ref> He also made 29 appearances for Stockton during the [[2023–24 NBA G League season]].<ref name="realgm" />

Jones played for the Sacramento Kings in the [[2024 NBA Summer League]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Sacramento Kings Announce NBA 2K25 Summer League Roster {{!}} Sacramento Kings |url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/sacramento-kings-announce-nba-2k25-summer-league-roster |access-date=5 September 2025 |work=www.nba.com |date=10 July 2024 |language=en}}</ref>

In the [[2024–25 Sacramento Kings season|2024–25 season]], Jones played 10 games for Sacramento<ref>{{cite web |title=Mason Jones 2024-25 Game Log |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/j/jonesma05/gamelog/2025/ |website=Basketball-Reference.com |access-date=5 September 2025 |language=en}}</ref> and 32 games for Stockton.<ref name="realgm" /> He helped Stockton win the 2024–25 [[List of NBA G League champions|NBA G League championship]] behind his [[NBA G League Finals MVP|Finals MVP]] performance.<ref>{{cite news |title=Stockton Kings Win First NBA G League Title in Franchise History |url=https://stockton.gleague.nba.com/news/stockton-kings-win-first-nba-g-league-title-in-franchise-history |access-date=5 September 2025 |work=Stockton Kings |date=15 April 2025 |language=en}}</ref><ref name=jones-named-finals-mvp>{{cite news |last1=Adams |first1=Luke |title=Stockton Kings Win G League Title, Mason Jones Named Finals MVP |url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2025/04/stockton-kings-win-g-league-title-mason-jones-named-finals-mvp.html |access-date=5 September 2025 |work=Hoops Rumors |date=15 April 2025}}</ref> In the three-game series against the [[Osceola Magic]], he averaged 22.3 points, 9.7 assists, 3.0 rebounds, and 2.7 steals per game and made 11-of-25 three-point shots (44.0%).<ref name="jones-named-finals-mvp" />

Jones played for the Sacramento Kings in the [[2025 NBA Summer League]].<ref name="realgm" />

===Perth Wildcats (2025)===
On September 8, 2025, Jones signed with the [[Perth Wildcats]] of the Australian [[National Basketball League (Australia)|National Basketball League]] for the [[2025–26 NBL season|2025–26 season]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Wildcats Sign Mason Jones: NBA G League Champ and Finals MVP |url=https://www.wildcats.com.au/news/wildcats-sign-mason-jones-nba-g-league-champ-and-finals-mvp |access-date=8 September 2025 |work=Wildcats.com.au |date=8 September 2025}}</ref> On October 17, he was released by the Wildcats after the team started the season with a 3–2 record.<ref>{{cite news |title=Perth Wildcats Statement: Mason Jones |url=https://www.wildcats.com.au/news/perth-wildcats-statement-mason-jones |access-date=17 October 2025 |work=Perth Wildcats |date=17 October 2025}}</ref>

===Hong Kong Bulls (2025–present)===
In December 2025, Jones joined the [[Hong Kong Bulls]] of the Chinese [[National Basketball League (China)|National Basketball League]].<ref name="Eurobasket" />
